chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Mutarraf, the mawla of Ma'an, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There are three things for the believer in which there is ease/comfort: a spacious house that conceals his nakedness and his poor condition from the people; and a righteous wife who assists him in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter; and a daughter or a sister whom he removes from his home either by her death or by marrying her off.

key_terms.سُوءَ حَالِهِ: His poor condition or state of poverty

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that bring ease to a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three sources of tranquility for the believer: a spacious home that preserves modesty and shields one’s private affairs from public scrutiny, a virtuous spouse who aids in both worldly and spiritual endeavors, and a daughter or sister whose marriage or death removes the burden of her maintenance and presence from the household. This narration highlights the socio-economic dimensions of domestic peace in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing privacy (*satr*) and familial relief as essential components of a believer's well-being.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Saeed Bin Janah, from Mutarraf, a slave of Ma’an, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘There are three (things) which are a best for the Believer – a spacious house to cover his nakedness and his evil state with from the people, and a righteous woman supporting him upon the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and a daughter or a sister exiting her from his home either when he dies or by getting her married off’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Sa‘id ibn Junah from Mutarrif Mawla’ Ma‘n who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Three things provide comfort for a believing person. Of such matters one is a spacious house which provides him privacy for his bad conditions among people, a virtuous wife who helps him in the matters of this and the next life and a daughter or sister whom he sends out of his house in marriage or death.’”
